items.entity: MBB supports (left edge and bottom-right corner)
items.description: App. C only states 'standard MBB beam boundary conditions [17]'; the restrained DOFs are never written out and no BC figure is available. The top-left load implies the symmetric half-beam, but the symmetry condition on the left edge and the type of the bottom-right support are left to the reference.
readings: Half-beam: u_x = 0 on all left-edge nodes (symmetry) + u_y = 0 only at the bottom-right corner node (roller), as in the 99/88-line codes
Half-beam: u_x = 0 on left edge + bottom-right corner node pinned (u_x = u_y = 0)

items.entity: bottom-right vertical support
items.description: How far the right-end support extends (one corner node or several bottom-edge nodes) is not stated; App. C only refers to the 'standard' MBB of [17].
readings: Single node at the bottom-right corner (x = L, y = 0)
Small patch of bottom-edge nodes at the right end (e.g., last 2-3 nodes)

items.entity: unit point load at top-left node
items.description: App. C gives magnitude (unit) and location (top-left node) but not the direction; the standard MBB implies vertical downward.
readings: Vertical downward, F_y = -1 (standard MBB)
Vertical upward, F_y = +1 (identical compliance and layout by linearity)

items.entity: physical dimensions / element size of the 144 x 48 domain
items.description: Only the element counts Nx x Ny = 144 x 48 are given (App. C). Element size and aspect ratio, physical length/height, and the length unit of r_min (2.0; bounds 1.5-10) are not stated. Square elements giving a 3:1 half-beam are implied, not stated.
readings: Unit square elements: L x H = 144 x 48, r_min measured in element widths
Normalized 3 x 1 domain (h = 1/48) with r_min still counted in element widths

items.entity: plane-stress thickness
items.description: App. C states plane-stress Q4 elements with E = 1, nu = 0.3, Emin = 1e-6, but never gives the out-of-plane thickness.
readings: Unit thickness t = 1
Other uniform thickness t (compliance scales as 1/t)

items.entity: 30% volume constraint - which density field it applies to
items.description: Eq. (14) imposes sum v_i rho~_i = V0 on the sigmoid output rho~, i.e., before the density filter and Heaviside projection that produce the FEA density. App. C only says 'target volume fraction 30%'. The physical design is at 30% only if eta_h comes from volume-preserving bisection, and the text does not say which option is used.
readings: Volume fraction 0.30 enforced on the physical (filtered + projected) densities, as in a standard solver
0.30 enforced only on the pre-filter field rho~; physical volume allowed to drift (eta_h = 0.5 fixed)

items.entity: Heaviside threshold eta_h
items.description: After Eq. (17): eta_h is 'either determined via bisection to enforce volume conservation across the projection or fixed to 0.5'. The option used for the MBB / Fig. 5 runs is never stated.
readings: eta_h found by bisection at every iteration (volume-preserving)
eta_h = 0.5 fixed

items.entity: filter radius lower bound (final r_min)
items.description: Sec. 5.1 says r_min converges to its lower bound 'set to r_min = 2.0 to prevent checkerboard patterns', while Table 1 lists r_min bounds [1.5, 10.0].
readings: Lower bound 2.0, final r_min = 2.0
Lower bound 1.5, final r_min = 1.5

items.entity: initial filter radius r_min^(0) and its schedule (four-hyperparameter runs)
items.description: r_min is tuned in the Fig. 5 runs. Its starting value is not given (r_min = 2.0 is stated only for the 2-D landscape study), and its evolution is shown only in Fig. 5d.
readings: r_min^(0) = 2.0 (landscape value)
r_min^(0) = 3.0, then decreasing to the bound
r_min^(0) at the middle of the Table 1 range (about 5.75)

items.entity: SIMP penalty p in the Fig. 5 runs
items.description: p is a tuned upper-level variable in [1, 10] (Table 1). Its initial value is not stated (p = 3 is given only for the landscape study and App. C.2), and the learned schedule and final value appear only in Fig. 5d.
readings: p^(0) = 3, then the learned schedule (final value read from Fig. 5d)
p^(0) = 1 (lower bound, continuation-like start)
Fixed p = 3 throughout

items.entity: Heaviside sharpness beta in the Fig. 5 runs
items.description: The BOTH runs use '4 values of beta^(0)' (Sec. 5.1), which are never listed. The learned schedule (small for most of the run, rising late) appears only in Fig. 5d. Bounds are [0.05, 15].
readings: beta^(0) spread over the bounds, e.g., {0.05, 5, 10, 15}
Small beta (about 1) for most of the run, ramped toward 15 at the end

items.entity: sigmoidal projection Phi with volume bisection
items.description: Sec. 5: the values entering 'a parametric sigmoidal projection Phi' are 'mapped to [0,1]' and the sigmoid is 'adaptively shifted via bisection'. The sigmoid's form and steepness, and whether a normalization is applied first, are not given (deferred to [14]).
readings: Unit-slope logistic rho~ = 1/(1+exp(-(x+b))), shift b found by bisection (as in [14])
Logistic with an unspecified steepness factor s != 1
Min-max normalization of x to [0,1], then a shifted sigmoid

items.entity: lower-level Adam optimizer settings
items.description: The Adam moment coefficients beta1 and beta2 are never given (only tau1 = tau2 = 1e-8). The lower-level learning rate starts at '~1e-8' from the probe (App. C), and its learned schedule appears only in Fig. 5d.
readings: beta1 = 0.9, beta2 = 0.999, eta^(0) = 0.5*eta* from re-running the App. A.4 probe

items.entity: computational budget / termination of the BOTH runs
items.description: B_max for the MBB runs is not stated; it is visible only on the Fig. 5a axis. Its unit is also inconsistent: Sec. 3 and App. A.1 count 'cumulative LL iterations', but Alg. 1 adds 4t+2 per upper-level update, which App. C.3 calls linear solves, and Fig. 5a plots linear solves.
readings: Budget counted in cumulative lower-level iterations (t per upper-level update)
Budget counted in linear solves (4t+2 per upper-level update), value read from Fig. 5a

items.entity: lower-level horizon t_start / t_max
items.description: Sec. 3 says t_start is 'typically set to 1 or 2' (t = 2 is advised for upper-level variables with no direct term, e.g., eta and p). The value used for Fig. 5 is not stated. t_max = 10 is given in Sec. 3, but the SMD example used 5.
readings: t_start = 1, t_max = 10
t_start = 2, t_max = 10

items.entity: upper-level normalization constants c_ref, d_ref
items.description: Eq. (18) and App. C: c_ref and d_ref are 'calculated based on a random network initialization and kept fixed', but their values and the seed and hyperparameters used are not given. They set the compliance-discreteness trade-off that drives the tuned beta, p, r_min and eta.
readings: c_ref = c(x0), d_ref = D(rho0) of one fixed random CNN initialization at the initial hyperparameters
c_ref, d_ref chosen per run so that both terms equal 1 at that run's start

items.entity: CNN reparameterization architecture
items.description: App. C.1: a dense layer produces (Nx/8, Ny/8, 32), then 'five successive hidden layers' each 'double the spatial resolution' until (Nx, Ny) is reached. Five doublings of 18x6 would give 576x192; only three fit. Kernel size, channel widths and output activation are deferred to [14].
readings: As in [14]: 5 conv layers with upsampling factors (1,2,2,2,1), 5x5 kernels, filters (128,64,32,16,1), no activation on the output
3 hidden layers, each doubling the resolution (18x6 to 144x48)
As in [14] but with tanh also after the last layer (literal reading of App. C.1)

items.entity: CNN initialization (initial design field)
items.description: Five network initializations are used (Sec. 5.1), but the seeds, the weight-initialization scheme and the initialization of the 128-dimensional trainable latent vector are not given. These set the initial density field.
readings: Defaults of the [14] code (variance-scaling conv init, latent ~ N(0,1)), seeds 0-4
Another initialization scheme or scale (e.g., Glorot uniform, different latent scale)

items.entity: number of BO/BOTH runs and network initializations
items.description: Sec. 5.1 says BO is repeated with '4 random seeds and five neural network initializations per seed, giving 24 runs' (4x5 = 20). App. C.3 says '8 independent BO trials per network initialization (three initializations), giving 24'. BOTH uses 5 initializations x 4 beta^(0) = 20 runs.
readings: BO: 4 seeds x 5 network initializations = 20 runs
BO: 8 seeds x 3 network initializations = 24 runs

items.entity: final-design evaluation for Fig. 5b/5c
items.description: App. C.2 says final designs are projected at beta = 64 before evaluation in the beta ablation (Fig. 14b). It does not say whether the Fig. 5 designs and their c* (at p = 1) and D values were also re-projected at beta = 64 or evaluated at the final learned beta.
readings: Evaluate at the final learned lower-level beta (no post-projection)
Re-project at beta = 64 before computing c* and D

locator: Sec. 5, the MBB beam (Appendix C, Fig. 5)
